minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission approved August minutes, reviewed the back-lot expansion bid timing, and moved its maintenance rules toward a separate policy.
minutes.summary: The commission approved the prior minutes, heard a resident urge green burial and volunteer landscaping, and was told the North Cemetery back-lot expansion spec is ready to go to procurement, with work hoped to be substantially done by December. Members compared proposed rules and regulations against Chapter 310 and agreed in general to keep maintenance policy separate from the public-facing rules, with Copilot-assisted merging to follow. The next meeting was moved from October 29 to Wednesday October 28.

public_comment.topic: Urged eco-friendly green burials and biodiverse, lower-mowing landscaping at the North Cemetery back lot expansion, native trees, and offered to volunteer.
A member of the public recommended mulching planting areas and planting smaller or bare-root native trees rather than large ones, and offered to donate seedlings.
A member of the public asked whether natural burials face the same wetland rules, and shared a Green Burial Council link and information on natural burial methods.

budget_items.what_was_said: An updated estimate came back the same as last time; the chair is fairly confident capital funds plus commission-allocated funds will cover it, and a late-season bid might come in lower.

budget_items.topic: Wetlands protection work in the contract
budget_items.what_was_said: Conservation-required barrier and erosion work was already line-itemed in the expansion contract.
No budget report was run and no money has been spent recently; spending will begin when soil is moved.
The DPW pays for outside landscaping help from its operating budget, not the commission's.
The fee schedule is considered done and should be in the rules so the commission does not miss extra funds.

decisions.decision: The chair will contact the contractor to learn the status of the long-delayed one-headstone repair.
The commission will run the tree list by a library trustee and favored smaller native trees for the planting.
Maintenance policy will be kept separate from the public-facing Chapter 310 rules; a member will merge the versions using Copilot and bring them back.
Natural burial will be explored over time, including talking to a neighboring DPW director; no near-term action as conventional inventory is ample.
The next meeting is moved to Wednesday the 28th instead of Thursday the 29th, pending availability.

what_happened.line: The commission moved to keep its maintenance policy separate from the public-facing Chapter 310 rules, with a member to merge the versions using Copilot and bring them back.
The commission was told the North Cemetery back-lot expansion spec is ready for procurement, with work hoped to be substantially done by December.
An updated cost estimate for the expansion came back unchanged, and the chair expects capital funds plus commission-allocated funds to cover it.
The commission will explore natural burial over time, including talking to a neighboring DPW director, with no near-term action because conventional inventory is ample.
The next meeting was moved to Wednesday the 28th instead of Thursday the 29th, pending availability.

why_it_matters: The back-lot expansion adds burial space and is paid from capital funds and commission-allocated funds, so the bid result decides whether those funds cover it.
The rules and fee schedule residents are charged under are being rewritten, and the commission treated the fee schedule as done and to be placed in the rules.
Residents asking for green burial or native landscaping heard that natural burial will be explored over time, with no near-term action, so near-term changes should not be expected.
watch_next: The next meeting, moved to Wednesday October 28, pending availability, where the merged rules and maintenance policy are due back.
The procurement bid for the back-lot expansion, which could come in lower if let late in the season.
